title: What is the class-loader delegation model?
shortTitle: What is the class-loader delegation model?
keyPoints: Parent-first delegation: each class loader asks its parent before trying to load a class itself
Application → Platform → Bootstrap: the chain goes up before trying locally
This prevents duplicate loading: java.lang.String is always loaded by Bootstrap, never by your code
If no parent can load the class, the originating class loader tries, then throws ClassNotFoundException
This model ensures security: you cannot create a fake java.lang.String in your classpath

s1_definition.oneliner: Each class loader delegates to its parent first. Only if the parent cannot find the class does the child try. This prevents duplicate loading and ensures core classes always come from Bootstrap.
s1_definition.profdef:
Delegation model:

- **Request goes up:** Application → Platform → Bootstrap.
- **Bootstrap tries first.** If it has the class (java.lang.String), it loads it. Done.
- **If not found, Platform tries.** If it has the class, it loads it.
- **If not found, Application tries.** Looks in the classpath.
- **If nobody has it:** ClassNotFoundException.
s1_definition.analogy: A bank branch (Application) receives a request for a form. Before printing its own, it asks the regional office (Platform). The regional office asks the head office (Bootstrap). If the head office has it, everyone uses that version. Only if nobody has it does the branch look in its own files.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Delegation chain (parent-first):

  Application CL → requests Account.class
    ↑ delegate to
  Platform CL → does not have Account
    ↑ delegate to
  Bootstrap CL → does not have Account
    ↓ return: not found
  Platform CL → not found
    ↓ return: not found
  Application CL → searches classpath → found → loads

  Security: you CANNOT replace java.lang.String
  because Bootstrap always loads it first.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The class-loader delegation model means each loader asks its parent before trying itself. This ensures core classes always come from Bootstrap, prevents duplicate loading, and blocks malicious replacements of JDK classes.

One sentence to remember: parent-first delegation means Bootstrap loads core classes, Platform loads extensions, and Application loads your code – in that order, always.
